headline: Math benchmarks saturate while agents doing real work still lag
outlook: Math is where progress has been fastest: models closed 95% of the remaining headroom there over the last year, FrontierMath passed 90% in September, and GPT-6.1 Sol has now posted a perfect score on FrontierMath Tier 4. The agents and real-work category is the clearest laggard, closing only 34% of its headroom, with the Remote Labor Index at 21.2% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%, though APEX-Agents jumped to 82.4% in a run of late-September records. The underlying trends suggest that gap may narrow, since the length of tasks AI can handle has reached 17.4 hours and is doubling roughly every 4.1 months, which on current trends points to work-week-long tasks around December, while the price of GPQA-level performance has fallen from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens. Not everything follows the fits, however: Terminal-Bench and GeoBench are both stuck short of 90% months after their trends said they should have arrived. With past likely ranges catching the real date only 59% of the time and a typical miss of five months, the most reasonable expectation for the next year is cheaper, longer-running agents rather than any precise date for when they can handle most remote work.
